column1: # CHANNELS.tsv -- which TAG each published channel currently points at. Append-only.
# THE CHANNEL IS A POINTER, NOT A VERSION SUFFIX, and that is forced rather than chosen:
# Archipelago calls tuplize_version() on archipelago.json's world_version when it loads an apworld,
# and that raises on any prerelease form ('0.3.8-beta.1' -> ValueError). A suffix is a load-time
# crash, not a label. So every build keeps a strict X.Y.Z and a tag, and a channel names one.
# Promotion is a new ROW, never an edit: "when did stable last move, and to what" is a question
# somebody will ask after a bad release, and an overwritten cell cannot answer it.
# Measured cadence 2026-08-08 over 30 tags (v0.1 .. v0.3.7, 34 days): MEDIAN GAP 0.82 DAYS.
# Daily is not an aspiration here, it is what already happens -- which is why stable can be the
# newest tag rather than a slow-moving one, and why the skew this file exists to bound is ~1 day.

the first release announced in public. 🛑 THIS ROW WAS THE BLOCKER FOR deploy_wizard.sh --landing, which fetches from the STABLE tag: while stable pointed at v0.3.10 the landing page could not be deployed at all, because v0.3.10 has no wizard/landing.html. It also pays off a promotion owed since v0.3.11 -- stable sat on v0.3.10 through two tags while check_channels stayed green, because that gate verifies the pointer RESOLVES, not that it is current.

the SweepSlot / confine-surface window. Promoted the morning after the tag rather than at the next window-open, which is the first time this row has not been owed for a day or more -- it sat on v0.3.10 through two tags in August while check_channels stayed green, because that gate verifies the pointer RESOLVES, not that it is current. 🛑 deploy_wizard.sh --landing fetches from THIS row, so it now serves v0.4.1's wizard.

the hub-collapse + cross-game-locks window. Paid the morning after the tag, not at the next window-open. 🛑 stable had sat on v0.4.1 through TWO tags (v0.4.2, v0.4.3) while check_channels stayed green, because that gate verifies the pointer RESOLVES, not that it is current -- the same way it sat on v0.3.10 in August. deploy_wizard.sh --landing fetches from THIS row, so until now the public landing page was serving v0.4.1's wizard against a v0.4.3 build.

the wizard-defaults + surface-lattice window. ⭐ PAID AT THE WINDOW OPEN, in the same commit -- the first time this row has not lagged its tag. It sat on v0.4.1 through TWO tags in this month alone and on v0.3.10 through two more in the last, every time with check_channels green, because that gate asks whether the pointer RESOLVES and never whether it is CURRENT. deploy_wizard.sh --landing fetches from THIS row, so the lag was the public landing page serving an older wizard against a newer build -- which is exactly the shape of the defect the wizard work in this window went and fixed elsewhere.

the goal-withholding + seven-Great-Runes window. ⭐ PAID AT THE WINDOW OPEN for the SECOND WINDOW RUNNING, in the same commit -- v0.4.4's row was the first time it had not lagged, and one occurrence is a fluke rather than a habit. Before that it sat on v0.4.1 through TWO tags in August and on v0.3.10 through two more in July, every time with check_channels green, because that gate asks whether the pointer RESOLVES and never whether it is CURRENT. deploy_wizard.sh --landing fetches from THIS row, so the public landing page now serves v0.4.5's wizard -- the one that emits every option rather than only the ones you changed (#732).
